newsitem.title: USA: Motorola cuts 170 jobs at Austin semiconductor unit.
newsitem.headline: Motorola cuts 170 jobs at Austin semiconductor unit.

text.p: Motorola Inc. said Monday it cut 170 jobs at its semiconductor facility in Austin, Tex., as part of a continuing effort to reduce spending.

The dismissals followed the company's offer earlier this month of voluntary severance packages to about 6,000 manufacturing employees in its semiconductor unit. That offer was an extension of one made to non-manufacturing workers in the group in July.
"They are a reduction in work force," Dan Rogers, director of public affairs for the company's semiconductor sector, said of the latest job reductions. "We're continuing cost-cutting."
The jobs were cut from all categories of work, Rogers said, and included manufacturing, non-manufacturing, professional and technical employees.
He declined to say if the company did not get the necessary results from the previous offers. "These were involuntary," Rogers said.

Schaumberg, Ill.-based Motorola earlier this month reported a 58 percent drop in third-quarter earnings and said its semiconductor business, plagued by industry-wide overcapacity, essentially broke even.
It said it would take fourth-quarter charges of "several tens of millions of dollars" to pay for cost-cutting measures, including reductions in its work force.
In July, Motorola terminated 145 employees, also at its Austin facility. They were the company's first involuntary layoffs in more than a decade.
Motorola's stock lost $1 to end at $46.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
